result.summary: Raster layer research is done, and the full log is in /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/cartography/raster/notes.md. Summary of measured results. 3DEP hillshade has no tile cache, so 256 px tiles come from one exportImage call each. A Montana outline tile set costs about 29 MB (grey PNG, zooms 5 to 10) or 363 MB (zooms 5 to 12); grey JPEG is about 8 MB and 87 MB; the tinted rule is about twice the PNG size. Tiles join without visible seams. NLCD 2021 (WMS and WCS on the MRLC server) has all six requested classes in the Missoula box; statewide 240 m is about 2 MB, statewide 30 m about 25 to 35 MB compressed; palette land cover tiles are about 5 to 9 KB each. The USGS shaded relief cache has no tiles at zooms 9 to 11 in the probed areas, so it cannot serve as a full pyramid; the hydro cache covers zooms 5 to 12. The USGS terms pages are blocked (403 from the CDN) and were not re-checked; quotes from earlier repo evidence are labelled as such. All estimates come from 2 to 8 sample tiles per zoom and are marked partly verified. Downloads total under 60 MB; the two large NLCD GeoTIFFs were deleted after measuring, and their checksums are in the notes.
blockers: www.usgs.gov returns HTTP 403 from its CDN to this session (FAQ, copyrights and 3DEP pages). It was not retried or routed around. The USGS terms sentences are from earlier repo evidence and are not re-checked live.

The USGS shaded relief cache returns 404 for every neighbouring tile at zooms 9 to 11 at Missoula and at zooms 9 and 10 at a second site, so it cannot be used as a complete pyramid without a fallback.
The Annual NLCD CONUS download was not measured (size unknown); statewide NLCD volumes use the NLCD 2021 product.
Tile size estimates rest on 2 to 8 sample tiles per zoom (standard error 7 to 27 percent per zoom mean); totals are estimates, not counts of produced files.

NLCD service grid is 30 map units in EPSG:3857 (about 20.5 m on the ground); the 240 m statewide grid was made by nearest-neighbour resampling through WMS, so a mode resample would change the size and class shares.
No browser or visual check of the tinted or palette tiles; only the seam mosaic was viewed. Nothing was published or shipped, and no git commands were run.

result.summary: Public-domain vector sources for the Montana base map, each checked live. Water: TIGER/Line 2026 county files (Missoula: 1,843 area and 8,702 line features, abbreviated names such as "Clark Fork Riv" and "Rattlesnake Crk", no GNIS IDs) and the USGS NHD service (Missoula: 21,019 large-scale flowlines, 6,720 with GNIS names such as "Clark Fork" and "Bitterroot River"); the whole-state NHD file is 592 MB zipped. Reservations: TIGER AIANNH gives 7 Montana reservations and 7 trust-land polygons, English names only (no Salish name in any file checked). Forests: the Forest Service EDW layer gives 7 Montana forests with most of their area in the state (Beaverhead-Deerlodge, Custer Gallatin, Helena-Lewis and Clark, Flathead, Lolo, Kootenai, Bitterroot). Parks and landmarks: TIGER area and point landmarks give named parks, schools, hospitals and airports; PAD-US could not be read from this session; TIGER has only 6 places of worship statewide. Places and peaks: TIGER 2026 has 497 places (127 incorporated, 370 CDPs); 2020 Census counts (Missoula 73,489; Lolo 4,399; Hamilton 4,659) and 2024 estimates are in hand; the Census API now needs a key. GNIS Montana has 3,181 summits and 1,870 populated places but no elevation column, so summit elevations were not counted. Routes: TIGER primary and secondary road names carry route numbers per segment (State Hwy 200, US Hwy 12, I- 90 Bus); the Montana State Library centreline layer carries them in two fields (type and number) but is not edge-matched. Licences: USGS and Census data are public domain with credit requested; the Census asks that TIGER/Line not be used inside a product name; the Forest Service and Montana State Library give no public-domain statement, so treat those two as open.
blockers: notes.md was not written: the subagent rule against report .md files overrides the workflow's request. The commands are in scripts/, the counts in logs/, and the quotes in the claims below.

PAD-US Montana was not read. Both ScienceBase download links return a web page (4,255 bytes) or a 403 from the storage bucket to this client. Park names come from TIGER instead, so PAD-US owner and access fields are missing.
Summit elevations cannot be counted: the GNIS Montana text file has no elevation column (21 columns).
Church icons need another public source: TIGER 2026 has 6 places of worship statewide and the GNIS Montana file has no church class.
Loyola Sacred Heart High School is in neither TIGER landmark file. Sacajawea Park (K2180) is in Lake County, not Missoula. McDonald Peak is in Lake County in GNIS (47.38252 N, 113.91900 W).
The Salish-language name for the Flathead Reservation is not in any file checked. It needs confirmation from the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes.
Licence gaps: the Montana State Library licence text is a disclaimer with no reuse grant; the Forest Service metadata has no public-domain statement. Ask both before publishing those layers.

The USGS copyright wording came through the fetch tool, because curl got 403 from this session. Check the exact sentences before publishing. The census.gov copyright page timed out twice; the TIGER/Line tech document text (local copy) was used instead.
NHD counts are service counts: the Montana outline for the state, a bounding box for Missoula. The 592 MB state geodatabase was not downloaded.
TIGER AREAWATER for county 30099 returned no Content-Length, so the statewide water total covers 55 of 56 area files.
The statewide Montana State Library count (238,661 segments) is from the map service; no bulk file was measured, and the service warns of gaps, overlaps and duplicates.
I-115 and I-315 appear in the Montana primary road intersect list and were not checked. The Turtle Mountain trust-land polygon touches Montana; its share inside the state was not measured.

Download budget: 78.8 MB logged in logs/downloads.jsonl (two failed PAD-US attempts included); about 5.3 GB disk free after removing the 38 MB primary roads zip and other large files already measured. The private venv (486 MB) is kept under the vector folder and can be removed.

result.method: Script: /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/cartography/render/proof_render.py, four steps (fetch, render, composite, measure), run with /home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python -I. Inputs, all in EPSG:3857 with pixel grids set from the zoom and the 2x scale: 3DEP exportImage (Hillshade Gray) for the owner box at 1600 px (fetched and checked; not used in the pictures), the region frame (780 by 1688) and the city box (1456 by 1448); NLCD 2021 through the MRLC WCS 1.0.0 GeoTIFF (region frame at 3x, reduced to 1x by a box average of one-hot classes, which is the mode; city box at native cells, one-hot bilinear then argmax); NLCD for the owner full box (1600 by 1430, fetched and checked); Census TIGER/Line 2026 (Missoula County roads; Montana primary and secondary roads); Census cartographic boundaries 2024 (reservations, places); Forest Service administrative forests (ArcGIS query in EPSG:3857, generalised at 60 m). Read only from the website repo: basemap.json (rivers, lakes, counties) and towns.json. Fonts: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 600 and 700 woff2 files, converted to TTF with fontTools. Drawing: 2x supersampling, Lanczos reduction. Palette from the style.css tokens (paper, ink, sky-700, violet-700) plus new soft colours: forest #cde2c3, cream developed #f5f1e6 to #e5d6b5, water #b9d9f2. Hillshade multiplied at strength 0.28. Labels and shields placed in Python with a collision test (areas first, then rivers and lakes, towns by rank, shields last). Measurement: zooms 5 to 12, 256 px tiles that touch the Montana outline (basemap land polygon in EPSG:3857); a stratified sample of six tiles per zoom (one random tile per cell of a 2 by 3 grid; all four tiles at zoom 5); each sample tile downloaded as an NLCD WCS 256 px tile and a 3DEP 256 px hillshade, then rendered as tint PNG, hillshade PNG, combined base PNG and WebP, plus clipped basemap vector JSON. Checks: each download was opened and checked (NLCD codes only, PNG grey ranges, TIFF tags, ZIP and JSON signatures), feature and file counts were read with python -I, and licence sentences were read from the files or pages named in sources.json. The script, measurements.json and sources.json contain no dashes and no model or vendor names (one ArcGIS parameter name carries a vendor name; the service requires it). Product build would differ: (1) render the base raster offline per zoom with mode resampling of the official 30 m NLCD grid, and store it as WebP (about 14 times smaller than PNG here) rather than PNG; (2) keep the basemap vector file for overview zooms, and add local streets and names only from zoom 12 or 13, from a generalised extract of the Montana State Library streets (the statewide zip is 117,639,105 bytes; the site's streets layer already starts at zoom 13); (3) replace the 10 m Natural Earth rivers with a finer river source, checked for licence first; (4) pick place names by size and zoom in the build, and thin the 47 names shown in the region frame; (5) place labels, shields and area names in the build with the same collision test, so the browser only draws them; (6) add the dark palette tokens and check text contrast against the site rule of 4.5 to 1, which this proof did not do; (7) add landmark icons, parks and peaks from checked public-domain point sources (none were fetched here); (8) choose the NLCD grid on purpose: the WCS serves a Web Mercator grid of 30 map units, about 20 m on the ground at 47 N, not the 30 m Albers grid.
result.statewide_estimate: Montana tiles (256 px) that touch the state outline, zooms 5 to 12: 4, 9, 22, 56, 178, 612, 2,254 and 8,852; 11,987 in total (14,520 in the bounding boxes). Refuted on two points. Everything else in P3 stands.

(1) Licence misread for the landmark layers. The claim's licence line is the general TIGER/Line citation text, and it presents the landmark layers as a public-domain source for the map. The Use Constraints field in the claimed file's own metadata continues: "The point landmark information in the TIGER/Line Shapefiles are for statistical data collection purposes only." That sentence limits the point landmarks to statistical data collection, so "public domain, free to use" does not settle whether they can be shown on a public map. This needs a legal read before the landmark layer ships. I could not read the text the claim cites as W1, so this compares the claim's licence line with the metadata inside the zip.

(2) The Missoula count is wrong against the proper county boundary. The 603 figure reproduces only with the Census 20 m cartographic outline, whose metadata says "Files should not be used for determining precise geographic area relationships."
